text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS @

- Chief Prosecutor Kalman Gyorgyi on Friday forwarded a petition to the Speaker of Parliament requesting that the parliamentry immunity of the Socialist Party treasurer, Laszlo Boldvai, be lifted. Several papers report that the case is linked to the privatisation scandal involving Marta Tocsik.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn expressed dissatisfaction with various aspects of police work on Friday and called for greater cooperation within the ranks to address areas of concern. (Sat.) @
- The European Commission encourages the government of Hungary to step up the pace of its work toward EU integration, said Hans van den Broek, the Union's commissioner for foreign affairs. (Sat.)

- Despite Parliament's approval last week of a conceptual framework for the country's new constitution, there is "practically no chance" that a new document will be passed into law during the current legislative cycle, Speaker Zoltan Gal said. (Sat.) @

- Three opposition parties announced that they will jointly petition the Constitutional Court to review a package of amendments to the privatisation law if President Arpad Goncz signs the bill. (Sat.)

- Christian Democratic People's Party vice president Tibor Fuzessy called on Janos Latorcai, chairman of the party's national board, and Tamas Isepy, parliamentary caucus leader, to resign their posts and leave the party.
- Moody's credit rating agency elevated Hungarian state debt to investment grade status on Friday, bringing its evaluation into line with those of other major agencies. (Sat.) @

- A consortium comprising the EBRD and 13 West European and Hungarian banks has suspended financing of the construction of Route M15, to run from the M1 motorway due to a November 19 court ruling that the toll collected on a stretch of the M1 is unreasonably high.

- It will take Eastern Europe longer than expected to catch up with the West, since economic growth in the reform countries will further slow down, according to a report by the Vienna institute for comparative economic studies WIIW. @
- As of Sunday night police in Miskolc had yet to question the young man severely injured around 7 p.m. Saturday when an explosive device blew up in his hands outside a disco.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The current account deficit grew by $20 million in October, bringing the total to $1.124 billion in the first ten months of the year, $1 billion less than in the same period of last year. (Sat.) @
- Friday was a record-smashing day at the Budapest Stock Exchange as the BUX index soared beyond the 4,000 point mark and the volume of trading hit a new high of more than HUF 3 billion. (Sat.)
- The Hungarian airline Malev will be further privatised by an equity raise carried out in several steps.
- Trading in Eravis shares at the Budapest Stock Exchange was suspended on Friday.
- Nine major Hungarian companies signed an agreement to establish a joint telecommunications company to be called PanTel. @
NEPSZABADSAG
- Police have arrested a high-ranking customs official on suspicion of abuse of authority and tax fraud.
